criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and municipal drinking-water supply and sewerage/sanitation service access across the 13 municipalities of the Metropolitan Region of Maceio (Block A, Alagoas, Brazil).
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, it analyses legal, institutional, regulatory, and governance reforms (Law 14.026/2020, Alagoas State Law 8.358/2020, regionalisation, and private-equity concession governance). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it directly examines utility ownership and regulatory structure governing service access (regionalised private-equity concession operated by BRK Ambiental/Brookfield, weakened municipal/state regulatory oversight by Arsal, and federal standardisation under ANA) as well as tariff and cost-recovery rules (highest-concession-fee auction rules, debenture debt servicing through consumer tariffs, real tariff adjustments for 0-10 m3 consumption, and fiduciary assignment of tariff receivables).
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical extreme-case study combining quantitative before-and-after comparison of municipal water and sanitation indicators (SNIS 2019 vs. SINISA 2023/2024 across 13 municipalities), inflation-adjusted tariff analysis (2021-2025), corporate financial/credit-rating analysis, and thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2006) of contractual documents, regulatory resolutions, and 55 news articles.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports concrete service access, reliability, and affordability outcomes: municipal water supply coverage (including post-concession coverage declines in 6 of 13 municipalities and 85% overall water coverage in 2024), sewerage network coverage (32% in 2023 vs. 49.2% contractual target; zero sewerage in 6 smaller municipalities), formal customer complaint rates for water shortages and leaks (>15% of active connections in 8 of 13 municipalities; >12,000 complaints in 2023), and a 31.27% real tariff increase (2021-2025, 0-10 m3 bracket).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (13 municipalities with 1,330,905 inhabitants in Block A, Metropolitan Region of Maceio, Alagoas, plus utility-level analysis of BRK Ambiental), exposure (financialised water/sanitation privatisation and regulatory/tariff structure under Law 14.026/2020), outcomes (water coverage, sewerage coverage, shortage complaint rates, real tariffs), and study design (mixed-methods empirical single-case study with pre-post municipal indicator comparison and thematic document analysis) are all clearly identified.

evidence_quotes.quote: The case study provides empirical evidence on how financialisation operates within WSS. It identifies the concrete mechanisms through which financialisation reshapes service provision, including high leverage, debt servicing through tariffs, and the assetisation of future revenue streams.
We also compared water and sanitation provision indicators from before privatisation (SNIS, 2019) and after (SINISA, 2024) in all the municipalities covered by the contract.

Only six municipalities in block A have water coverage over 90%, indicating that progress towards universalisation remains uneven and insufficient. Satuba stands out as a case in point, with only 50% of the urban population having access to piped water (SINISA, 2025; SNIS, 2019).
In terms of sanitation, the contract set a target of achieving 49.2% coverage by the end of 2023. However, data show that only 32% of the Block A population was served by sewerage in 2023.

In 2023, only five out of the 13 municipalities in Block A managed to keep this complaint rate, measured as the number of formal grievances relative to the total number of active connections, below 15%, a threshold that reflects a systemic failure in a regulated utility where continuous supply is expected.

From the public side, one of the reasons for that is the change in the national regulatory framework, with Law 14.026/2020 establishing that the National Agency for Waters and Basic Sanitation (ANA) has the role of standardising regulation to ensure legal security to contracts.

raw_response.exposure: Financialised water and sanitation utility privatisation (regionalised 35-year concession awarded to private-equity-owned BRK Ambiental under Federal Law 14.026/2020 and Alagoas State Law 8.358/2020, incorporating highest-concession-fee auction rules, debenture-backed debt-service tariff rules, fiduciary assignment of receivables, and centralised/weakened regulatory oversight).
raw_response.outcome: Municipal water supply coverage, sewerage network coverage, formal customer complaint rates regarding water shortages and leaks, and real residential water tariff increases (0-10 m3 bracket).
raw_response.population_and_sample: 13 municipalities in Block A (Metropolitan Region of Maceio, Alagoas, Brazil; total population 1,330,905 inhabitants) and the private concessionaire utility BRK Ambiental S.A. (analysed using SNIS 2019 and SINISA 2023/2024 municipal indicators, 2021-2025 tariff schedules, financial/credit reports, and 55 news articles).
raw_response.rationale: Full-text empirical case study examining how utility ownership, concession contracting, regulatory restructuring (Law 14.026/2020), and tariff/cost-recovery rules under financialised water privatisation in Maceio, Brazil affect municipal water supply coverage, sewerage coverage, water shortage complaint rates, and tariff affordability. Meets all inclusion criteria (c1-c6) under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2.
raw_response.study_design: Mixed-methods empirical case study (extreme-case design combining pre-post municipal indicator comparison from SNIS 2019 and SINISA 2023/2024, inflation-adjusted tariff and corporate financial analysis, and Braun & Clarke thematic analysis of contractual, regulatory, and media documents)
